A specific PEP monitoring rule in the transaction monitoring system generates an alert when a PEP makes or receives a single payment exceeding €10,000 (low-risk country), €5,000 (medium-risk country), or €2,500 (high-risk country), using the Country AML Risk Ranking for categorisation.
UBO data will be accessed via a dedicated, secure KvK portal where all searches are logged and auditable, ensuring traceability of UBO lookups.

Watchlist data (sourced from Comply Advantage via Incode) is downloaded daily and used to screen: (i) every new user at onboarding, (ii) the entire user base upon each datafile update including UBOs, and (iii) certain payments post-verification by Compliance operations.

Onboarding risk scorecard for Spanish resident users incorporates professional activity information (collected via a mandatory onboarding flow), scoring unemployed users +10 and students +5 based on FIU reporting rate data, in compliance with Spanish AML regulations.
When a user escalates an offboarding dispute to Kifid or initiates legal proceedings, the Legal team is mandatorily engaged to manage and guide the response process.

Continuous training programme for transaction monitoring analysts comprising: (i) regular meet-ups on new developments, (ii) a knowledge framework resource, and (iii) periodic knowledge exams to verify competence.

Automated authorization check (Dutch non-sole-proprietorship companies) verifies the account opener is a legal director or solely authorized via KvK data; failures and all non-Dutch companies are routed to manual director verification.

Automated company name check flags companies whose names contain words associated with increased risk profiles; for non-Dutch sole proprietorships, also flags mismatches between company name and director name.

Screening of transaction origin and destination countries, with mandatory flagging and blocking of transactions to or from sanctioned jurisdictions (e.g., Russia, Belarus, North Korea) or partially sanctioned territories (e.g., Crimea).
Acceptance policy rule prohibiting companies without shares from appearing in any layer other than the first layer of a corporate structure; violations result in denial.

The KYC system provides a dedicated Approval Checks section within each user's KYC History, enabling agents to view all failed checks for every approval, supporting auditability and structured review.
Automated and manual check to identify US persons among directors and UBOs, requiring a verified Social Security Number (SSN) and supporting documentation before account approval.
For every Dutch company onboarded, a Dutch UBO register extract is retrieved. If the register is unavailable, a Chamber of Commerce confirmation of UBO registration is requested as a fallback.

FIU reports filed due to failed CDD must include a description of the reasons for the CDD failure alongside the suspicious transaction details, ensuring complete and informative reporting in such cases.

Manual initial eligibility assessment by onboarding agents reviews all failed auto-approval checks to identify show-stoppers and determine whether to deny the application or proceed to the structure assessment.
STAKs (Stichting Administratiekantoor) and any company that has a STAK anywhere in its ownership structure are categorically rejected during onboarding.
Mandatory regular training on financial crime risks, sanctions regulations, and screening procedures for all personnel involved in screening and alert investigation.
Analysts must use the most recent version (amendment) of the applicable sanctions legislation/list to avoid acting on entries that have been removed, preventing false positive sanctions actions.
Automated legal guardianship check (Dutch companies) blocks account opening if the director is under legal guardianship.
Acceptance policy rule limiting corporate structures to a maximum of two layers, requiring the third layer to consist exclusively of natural persons; companies exceeding this are denied.
Automatic classification of PEPs, RCAs, and SIPs as at least high risk by the risk scoring model, regardless of other scoring factors.
During new account opening, staff must actively screen for U.S. person indicators including U.S. place of birth, U.S. current residence, and U.S. nationality to identify potential U.S. tax liability.
